name: Question 10
worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}+2y & =-x \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({y}^{2}+2y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-x) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2}+2y) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-x) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot (2y+2) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (-1) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot (2y+2) & =-\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting the given information $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=2$ and $x=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2(2y+2) & =-\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

We also want to substitute for $y,$ but we are not given this value. However, we can find it by substituting $x=1$ into the equation of the curve.

At the point where $x=1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}+2y & =-x \\ {y}^{2}+2y & =-1 \\ {y}^{2}+2y+1 & =0 \\ (y+1)^{2} & =0 \\ y & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $y=-1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2(2y+2) & =-\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\ 2(2\cdot (-1)+2) & =-\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\ 2(0) & =-\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\ 0 & =-\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

At the point where x=1, we have y2+2y=−xy2+2y=−1y2+2y+1=0(y+1)2=0y=−1.
